title: Structural and magnetic properties of TbCuAs$_2$ studied by X-ray and neutron scattering
authors: M. G. Kim, T. Heitmann, S. Boney, C. Neupane, R. Acevedo-Esteves, A. Sapkota, D. Evans, P. C. Canfield, C. Nelson, E. D. Mun, J. -W. Kim
abstract: We investigated antiferromagnetic metal TbCuAs$_2$, which exhibits an anomalous resistivity upturn at low temperatures. This resistivity upturn has been proposed to originate from the material's magnetic ground state; however, the precise nature of the antiferromagnetic ordering in this compound has not been previously established. Here, we present a combined single crystal neutron diffraction, X-ray resonant magnetic scattering, and single crystal X-ray diffraction study of TbCuAs$_2$. These measurements unambiguously determine the Tb magnetic moment direction, the antiferromagnetic arrangement along high symmetry directions, the interplay between structure and magnetism, and their temperature dependence. Our observations are compared with previous studies on sister compounds in the rare-earth copper arsenide family ($R$CuAs$_2$, $R$ = Sm and Gd), which also displays resistivity anomalies. We suggest a common underlying physics governing the structural and magentic properties of rare-earth copper arsenides that exhibit low-temperature resistivity anomalies.
summary: This experimental study characterizes the structural and magnetic ground state of the antiferromagnetic metal TbCuAs2 using neutron and X-ray scattering. The authors determined the magnetic structure to be incommensurate and aligned along the b-axis, confirming a strong coupling between the magnetic ordering and the crystal lattice distortion. The findings suggest a common physical mechanism governs the behavior of rare-earth copper arsenides exhibiting low-temperature resistivity anomalies.
main_problem: The study investigates the anomalous resistivity upturn observed at low temperatures in the antiferromagnetic metal TbCuAs2, and aims to determine the precise nature of its antiferromagnetic ordering and its interplay with the crystal structure.
main_result: The magnetic structure is unambiguously determined as $\Gamma_4$ with moments along the $b$ axis and a $(++--)$ stacking sequence along $c$, revealing a coupling between incommensurate magnetism and structural distortion.
method: The research employed a combination of single crystal neutron diffraction, X-ray resonant magnetic scattering (XRMS), and single crystal X-ray diffraction measurements.
model_or_system: The physical system is the rare-earth copper arsenide family, specifically TbCuAs2, which is an antiferromagnetic metal exhibiting low-temperature resistivity anomalies.
key_observables: Resistivity ($\rho$) vs. Temperature ($T$), magnetic scattering intensities (from XRMS and neutron diffraction), and lattice parameters ($c, a, b$) dependence on temperature.
important_parameters: Antiferromagnetic ordering temperature ($T_N \approx 10 \text{ K}$), incommensurate propagation vector $\mathbf{q} = (\tau, 0, 0.5)$ with $\tau \approx 0.3$.
main_assumptions: The analysis compares results to sister compounds in the $R\text{CuAs}_2$ family, suggesting a common underlying physics governs the structural and magnetic properties.
figures_summary: Figures summarize XRMS results confirming AFM ordering, magnetic peak positions, and the temperature dependence of lattice parameters ($c, a, b$).
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first establishing the anomalous resistivity upturn, then using XRMS and neutron diffraction to determine the magnetic ordering vector and moment direction, followed by analyzing the temperature dependence of both magnetic and structural parameters, and finally comparing these findings to related compounds.
why_interesting: The detailed structural and magnetic characterization of this strongly correlated material provides empirical evidence for coupled spin-lattice instabilities, which is relevant to understanding unconventional superconductivity mechanisms in related iron-based superconductors.
